about: Size ladder of pure open-source imports (permissive licenses), pinned commits. size_kb is GitHub's reported repository size; the script measures the packed size, objects and commits of the pinned commit and writes them to its results. Optional rungs run only when named with --rungs.

rungs.name: svelte
rungs.measured: 118.8 MiB packed, 168,943 objects, 11,458 commits (7,025 first-parent), 13,129 tip files and trees, largest blob 18.3 MB (site/static/tutorial/music/strauss.mp3)
expect: Import: 8 pushes planned (--plan-only); push 3 carries strauss.mp3 (18.3 MB > 16 MiB per object) and is expected to be refused, so reads run on the first 2 pushes' history.
Full clone: refused, 169k objects > the 40,000 a fetch sends (even of the partial history, likely).
Partial clone: likely refused (11k commits plus their trees > 40,000).
Search: first query builds the index cold (tens of seconds); later ones served. Blame, history, Overview: served.

rungs.name: kubernetes
expect: Import: 40-60 pushes (about 1.5 GB / 40 MiB; objects likely over 1M / 30k), hours of pushing; any blob over 16 MiB stops it.
Full and partial clone: refused (objects far over 40,000).
Shallow clone: the tip's files and trees, near 40,000 (borderline: refused if over).

Search: cold index build over many partitions may exceed a request's limits (first break expected here after clones). Overview, blame, history: served; history and blame on 142k commits test the authority's log size.

rungs.name: material-design-icons
expect: Import: about 130+ pushes by bytes (5 GB / 40 MiB) but only 318 commits: single first-parent steps of tens of thousands of icon files are expected to exceed one push (40,000 objects or 64 MiB): the import is expected to break here first.
Shallow clone: the tip holds far over 40,000 files: refused. Full and partial clone: refused.
Search: directories of more than 200,000 files are not indexed (named as refused); Overview lists the whole tree (large) but analyses at most 400 source files.

rungs.name: clickhouse
expect: Optional source-code rung over 5 GB (313k commits). Import: hundreds of pushes; same fetch caps as kubernetes; DO SQLite growth from 313k commits' records is the limit to watch.
